text: Nine quick ones to finish. Question eleven. What is the difference between a source test and a model test? A source test checks raw data as it lands, and points straight at ingestion. A model test guards your own logic. Do both. Question twelve. Where should tests live, at staging or in marts? Both. Staging tests catch upstream problems early; mart tests guard the grain and the metrics. Test only at the end, and a bug travels far before it's caught. Question thirteen. What is a data contract in dbt? An enforced declaration of a model's column names, types and constraints. If the sequel produces a different shape, the build fails, before any consumer sees it. Question fourteen. What is test severity, and when do you use warn versus error? Error, the default, fails the run: use it for invariants like a unique key. Warn logs and carries on, for soft signals. Thresholds can warn at one failing row and error at a hundred. Question fifteen. How do you avoid alert fatigue from noisy tests? Choose those severities deliberately, use the thresholds, and fix or delete tests that fail for known reasons. A suite that cries wolf gets ignored. Question sixteen. What extra tests do dbt utils and dbt expectations add? Accepted ranges, expressions that must hold, compound keys, row-count bounds and distribution checks: the sanity checks the four built-ins leave out. Question seventeen. What are dbt unit tests, and how do they differ from data tests? A unit test runs a model's logic on mocked rows and compares an expected output, so it runs in CI with no real data. Data tests check the real data in the warehouse. Question eighteen. What is store failures, and why enable it? It writes the failing rows to a table instead of just counting them, so a red check becomes a dataset you can query. Question nineteen. Why prefer fixing data upstream over patching it in a downstream model? A coalesce in one model hides the defect, has to be copied into every consumer, and anything reading the source still gets bad data. Fix it once, at the source. Tests check each model against what you expected of it. They can all pass while two dashboards disagree about revenue. Next: metrics and the semantic layer.
